name: failing-test
description: After a recent change to the billing service, order totals are coming out wrong and CI has gone red — the suite was green before today. Figure out what the change broke and fix it.
bugs: a refactor of compute_total dropped the per-item quantity: it sums item['price'] instead of item['price'] * item['qty'], so multi-quantity orders undercount
the same refactor also dropped the per-line discount: it ignores item['discount'] entirely, so a discounted line is overcharged (the line subtotal must be multiplied by (1 - discount) before tax)
the same refactor seeds the subtotal from items[0] and loops over items[1:], so an empty order raises IndexError instead of returning 0.0

regression_check.cmd: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '.'); from invoice import compute_total as f; assert f([], 0.08) == 0.0, f([], 0.08); assert f([{'price': 100.0, 'qty': 2, 'discount': 0.25}], 0.0) == 150.0, f([{'price': 100.0, 'qty': 2, 'discount': 0.25}], 0.0); assert f([{'price': 10.0, 'qty': 3, 'discount': 0.0}, {'price': 50.0, 'qty': 2, 'discount': 0.10}], 0.0) == 120.0, f([{'price': 10.0, 'qty': 3, 'discount': 0.0}, {'price': 50.0, 'qty': 2, 'discount': 0.10}], 0.0)"

correct_diagnosis: A recent refactor of compute_total dropped both the per-item quantity (summing price instead of price*qty) and the per-line discount (ignoring item['discount']), and it seeded the subtotal from items[0] while looping over items[1:]. So multi-quantity orders undercount, discounted lines overcharge, and an empty order raises IndexError. Summing item['price']*item['qty']*(1 - item.get('discount', 0)) over all items (which also returns 0.0 for an empty order) fixes all three.

reference_fix.description: Sum price*qty*(1 - discount) over all items via a comprehension, restoring the quantity and the per-line discount and making an empty order return 0.0.
reference_fix.cmd:
cat > invoice.py <<'EOF'
"""Invoice totals."""


def compute_total(items, tax_rate):
    """Total for an invoice: the sum of the line items, plus tax.

    items: list of line items. Each line item is a dict:
        {"price": float, "qty": int, "discount": float}
    where "discount" is an optional per-line fraction off (e.g. 0.10 for
    10% off that line) and defaults to 0 when absent. Discounts apply to
    the line subtotal (price * qty) before tax.
    tax_rate: e.g. 0.08 for 8%
    """
    subtotal = sum(
        item["price"] * item["qty"] * (1 - item.get("discount", 0))
        for item in items
    )
    return subtotal * (1 + tax_rate)
EOF

naive_fix.description: Trap bait: multiply each term by qty (passes the red test) but ignore the per-line discount field — a discounted order is overcharged, failing the held-out regression.
